newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian ruler backs production sharing for oil.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian ruler backs production sharing for oil.

text.p: Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha has approved in principle the adoption of production sharing contracts (PSCs) in future upstream oil activities with multinational firms, local newspapers reported on Friday.

Abacha, receiving the new managing director of Chevron Corp in Nigeria, George Kirkland, in the capital Abuja on Thursday, said the government would in the "near future" shift from the present joint venture partnerships to PSCs.
He said details of the conversion to PSCs from joint ventures were being worked out, the independent Thisday newspaper said.
Nigeria through state oil company Nigerian National Petroleum Corp currently holds an average of 57 percent in local units of multinationals that run the bulk of its oil industry.
The government has, however, been finding it difficult to pay its contribution or cash calls to the joint operations.
It currently owes about $1.2 billion in cash call arrears and this combined with the government's reduction of the operational budget of the joint ventures is affecting their oil exploration drive.
One of them, Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited, a joint venture with Mobil Corp, has had to terminate contracts with three rigs that were drilling for it in Nigeria.

Many oil industry executives consider PSCs a solution to Nigeria's inability to fund oil activities because under such contracts the oil companies pay fully for exploration and recoup their expenses when oil is struck.
Abacha said his government would show more interest in the oil sector and would study all projects by the joint venture partners more carefully to ensure they were viable and profitable.
